newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-MCCOLGAN QUITS TRACK FOR MARATHONS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-MCCOLGAN QUITS TRACK FOR MARATHONS.

text.p: Former 10,000 metres world champion Liz McColgan has quit the track scene to concentrate on marathon running, the Scottish long-distance runner said on Wednesday.
The decision means McColgan will not try to regain her title at the world championships in Athens in August.

"The track has been part of my life. It's a very hard decision to make not to go there any more but I think my best prospects and talent for the future lie in marathon running and I've just got to accept that being a marathon runner, I can't do anything and everything as well," McColgan told a news conference in Edinburgh.
The 33-year-old underwent a back operation last week and felt she would not be fit enough to compete in the world championship trials in Sheffield at the end of this month.
McColgan, who won a gold medal in the 10,000 metres at the 1991 championships in Tokyo, was in Edinburgh for the launch of the Great Caledonian Run on October 19 in which she will participate.
She will also compete in the Great North Run and Great South Run later in the year.
"The three races...are ideal preparation for the marathon. I now firmly believe this is my one and only distance for the future," McColgan said.
Her next international marathon is in Tokyo on November 30.
